fields.name: Aerospace Engineering
fields.summary: Aerospace engineers design, analyze, test, and certify aircraft, spacecraft, satellites, and propulsion systems for companies like Boeing, SpaceX, and Lockheed Martin.

pathway.title: Aerospace Engineer I / Design Engineer
pathway.description: Works under senior engineer supervision on component-level design, CAD modeling, and analysis (stress, aero, thermal); supports test campaigns and documentation for a single subsystem.

pathway.title: Aerospace Engineer II / Systems Engineer
pathway.description: Owns a subsystem or discipline area (e.g., propulsion, structures, avionics) with reduced oversight; runs trade studies, interfaces with suppliers, and contributes to design reviews.

pathway.title: Senior Aerospace Engineer / Lead Engineer
pathway.description: Leads a small engineering team or major subsystem across the full lifecycle, mentors junior engineers, owns technical risk and schedule for their area, and represents the team at program-level reviews.

pathway.title: Principal Engineer / Engineering Manager / Chief Engineer
pathway.description: Sets technical direction across a program or product line, manages engineers and budgets (or serves as technical authority in an IC track), and interfaces directly with customers (NASA, DoD, airlines) and executive leadership.

conferences: Farnborough International Airshow / Paris Air Show
organizations: AIAA (American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics)

media.title: Day In My Life as a NASA Engineer
media.description: A NASA JPL aerospace/electrical engineer walks through a real day of her engineering work and life.

media.title: The Aerospace Engineering Podcast
media.description: Interview-format show featuring conversations with aerospace engineers about their careers and technical work.

fields.name: Mechanical Engineering
fields.summary: Mechanical engineers design, analyze, and build physical systems and machines, from vehicles and aircraft to robotics and manufacturing equipment, spanning industries like aerospace, automotive, energy, and consumer products.

pathway.title: Mechanical Engineer I / Design Engineer
pathway.description: Works under supervision on component-level design, CAD modeling, testing, and documentation; builds fundamentals in tools like SolidWorks/CATIA and analysis methods while executing well-defined tasks.

pathway.title: Mechanical Engineer II / Design Engineer II
pathway.description: Owns subsystem design and analysis with less oversight, runs FEA/simulation studies, coordinates with manufacturing and suppliers, and begins mentoring junior engineers.

pathway.title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
pathway.description: Leads major project components or full small systems, makes independent technical trade-off decisions, reviews others' designs, and often pursues PE licensure to expand scope.

pathway.title: Principal Engineer / Engineering Manager
pathway.description: Sets engineering standards across programs, leads cross-functional technical strategy or manages a team, and represents engineering in major design reviews and business decisions.

conferences: ASME IMECE (International Mechanical Engineering Congress & Exposition)

media.title: Day in the Life of a Mechanical Engineer | Factory Life
media.description: A mechanical engineer who helped build a battery gigafactory shows a real factory-floor workday.

media.title: Being an Engineer
media.description: Established engineering-career podcast interviewing a mechanical engineer/manufacturing strategist about his career.

fields.name: Civil Engineering
fields.summary: Civil engineers design, build, and maintain the infrastructure that societies run on, roads, bridges, water systems, and buildings, moving from EIT to licensed PE as they take on greater project responsibility.

pathway.title: Staff Engineer / Engineer-in-Training (EIT)
pathway.description: Performs calculations, drafting/CAD, quantity takeoffs, and field observations under a licensed PE's supervision while studying for and taking the FE exam to earn EIT status.

pathway.title: Project Engineer
pathway.description: Manages design packages and permit documents, coordinates with contractors and architects, and begins sitting for the PE exam after accumulating the required years of supervised experience.

pathway.title: Licensed Civil Engineer / Project Manager (PE)
pathway.description: Now a licensed PE, owns full project scope, budget, and schedule; stamps drawings, manages client relationships, and reviews and mentors junior engineers.

pathway.title: Senior Project Manager / Principal / Associate
pathway.description: Directs multiple projects or a practice area, leads business development and proposals, carries P&L or client-relationship accountability, and sets technical standards across teams.

media.title: An ACTUAL Day In The Life of a CIVIL ENGINEER. Construction Site Engineer.
media.description: A real construction site engineer walks through an actual workday in the UK.

media.title: TCEP 311: Developing Leadership Skills In Civil Engineering
media.description: Episode of The Civil Engineering Podcast on building leadership and communication skills as a practicing civil engineer.

fields.name: Electrical Engineering
fields.summary: Electrical engineers design, test, and improve the systems that generate, distribute, and control electrical power and signals, from microchips to the power grid to EV drivetrains.

pathway.title: Associate / Electrical Engineer I
pathway.description: Works under senior engineer supervision on circuit design, testing, and documentation; builds prototypes and runs validation tests while learning company design standards.

pathway.title: Electrical Engineer II / Design Engineer
pathway.description: Owns discrete subsystems or components independently, interfaces with suppliers and cross-functional teams, and begins leading small design reviews.

pathway.title: Senior Electrical Engineer
pathway.description: Leads full projects end-to-end, mentors junior engineers, resolves complex design tradeoffs, and often begins pursuing PE licensure or specialization.

pathway.title: Principal Electrical Engineer / Engineering Lead
pathway.description: Serves as technical authority across multiple projects or a product line, sets design standards, drives architecture decisions, and influences engineering strategy.

fields.name: Computer Science / Software Engineering
fields.summary: Software engineers design, build, and maintain the applications, systems, and infrastructure that power modern products, with a career path that moves from writing well-scoped code to owning architecture and technical strategy.

pathway.title: Software Engineer I (SDE I / Junior SWE)
pathway.description: Writes and tests code on well-defined tasks under close mentorship, ramps on codebase and tooling, and contributes to small features or bug fixes with senior review.

pathway.title: Software Engineer II (SDE II)
pathway.description: Owns features end-to-end with less oversight, participates in design discussions, writes production-quality code and tests, and starts mentoring interns/new hires.

pathway.title: Senior Software Engineer (SDE III / Senior SWE)
pathway.description: Leads design and delivery of complex, cross-team projects, sets technical direction for a component or service, mentors other engineers, and is a go-to expert in their domain.

pathway.title: Staff / Principal Engineer
pathway.description: Drives architecture and technical strategy across multiple teams or the org, resolves ambiguous cross-cutting problems, influences roadmaps, and multiplies impact through mentorship and technical leadership.

fields.name: Chemical Engineering
fields.summary: Chemical engineers design, scale, and optimize the processes that turn raw materials into fuels, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and advanced materials.

pathway.title: Process Engineer I / Associate Chemical Engineer
pathway.description: Supports plant operations under supervision, monitors process data, runs small experiments/trials, writes SOPs, and assists with routine troubleshooting and safety reviews.

pathway.title: Process Engineer II / Project Engineer
pathway.description: Owns process areas independently, leads small capital or debottlenecking projects, performs mass/energy balance and P&ID work, and participates in HAZOP/process safety reviews.

pathway.title: Senior Process Engineer / Process Engineering Lead
pathway.description: Leads multi-discipline improvement or expansion projects, mentors junior engineers, manages vendor and contractor relationships, and drives yield, cost, and reliability targets across a unit.

pathway.title: Principal Engineer / Engineering Manager / Process Safety Fellow
pathway.description: Sets technical direction for a site or business unit, owns capital project portfolios, represents the company on process safety/regulatory matters, and manages engineering teams.

fields.name: Data Science & Statistics
fields.summary: Data scientists and statisticians turn raw data into predictive models, experiments, and decision-support tools that drive business and product strategy.

pathway.title: Data Scientist I / Data Analyst
pathway.description: Cleans and explores datasets, builds dashboards and basic statistical/ML models under close guidance, and translates stakeholder questions into well-scoped analyses.

pathway.title: Data Scientist II
pathway.description: Owns end-to-end projects (experiment design, modeling, deployment support), works directly with product/business partners, and starts mentoring junior analysts.

pathway.title: Senior Data Scientist
pathway.description: Leads cross-functional initiatives, sets technical direction for a domain (e.g., forecasting, personalization), reviews others' work, and influences roadmap decisions.

pathway.title: Staff/Principal Data Scientist (or Analytics Manager)
pathway.description: Defines technical strategy across teams, drives org-wide standards and high-impact bets, and either goes deep as a technical IC or moves into people management overseeing a data science team.

fields.name: Biomedical Engineering
fields.summary: Biomedical engineers apply engineering principles to design, test, and bring to market medical devices and diagnostics such as pacemakers, imaging systems, and surgical instruments.

pathway.title: R&D / Design Engineer I
pathway.description: Entry-level role doing hands-on design, prototyping, and testing of components/subsystems under senior engineer supervision, often supporting design verification and documentation for FDA submissions.

pathway.title: Design Engineer II / R&D Engineer
pathway.description: Owns design of subsystems or full devices, runs design verification/validation testing, and collaborates with regulatory and quality teams on 510(k)/PMA documentation with growing design autonomy.

pathway.title: Senior Design Engineer / Product Development Engineer
pathway.description: Leads cross-functional design projects end-to-end, mentors junior engineers, drives risk management (FMEA) and design controls, and interfaces directly with regulatory bodies and manufacturing partners.

pathway.title: Principal Engineer / Engineering Manager / Director of R&D
pathway.description: Sets technical strategy across a product line or platform, manages engineering teams and budgets, and represents R&D to executives, clinicians, and external partners on major program decisions.

mastersPrograms.name: Master of Engineering in MedTech Design

fields.name: Biotechnology / Pharmaceutical Sciences
fields.summary: Bench scientists in biotech/pharma design and run laboratory experiments that turn early discoveries into approved therapies, advancing from hands-on technician roles into experiment-owning, then program-leading positions.

pathway.title: Research Associate I
pathway.description: Executes established experimental protocols (cell culture, assays, PCR, etc.) under direct supervision; focuses on precise data collection and lab documentation rather than experimental design.

pathway.title: Research Associate II / Senior Research Associate
pathway.description: Works with greater independence, troubleshoots failed experiments, may train new hires, and starts contributing input to experimental design and small project workstreams.

pathway.title: Scientist I / Scientist
pathway.description: Independently designs and executes experiments, owns a defined project or workstream, interprets data, and presents findings to cross-functional teams (e.g., process development, regulatory).

pathway.title: Senior Scientist / Principal Scientist
pathway.description: Leads a research program or platform, sets scientific strategy and priorities, mentors junior scientists, and may begin managing a small team while remaining hands-on technically.

organizations: American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB)

fields.name: Public Health & Epidemiology
fields.summary: Public health professionals and epidemiologists investigate disease patterns and design data-driven policies and programs to protect population health across government, health systems, and nonprofits.

pathway.title: Epidemiologist I / Public Health Analyst
pathway.description: Conducts case investigations, data entry/cleaning, and basic surveillance reporting under supervision at a health department or health system; supports outbreak response and routine disease reporting.

pathway.title: Epidemiologist II
pathway.description: Independently manages surveillance systems and datasets, leads outbreak investigations, and produces epidemiological reports and analyses with growing autonomy over study design and statistical methods.

pathway.title: Senior Epidemiologist / Epidemiology Program Coordinator
pathway.description: Leads a disease program or research portfolio, designs studies and evaluation protocols, mentors junior epidemiologists, and represents the program to external partners and policymakers.

pathway.title: Epidemiology Program Director / Chief Epidemiologist
pathway.description: Sets strategic priorities and oversees budget and staffing for a division or program area, translates surveillance data into policy recommendations, and serves as the organization's senior technical authority.

majors.name: Aerospace Engineering
majors.summary: Aerospace engineering blends physics, math, and materials science to design aircraft, spacecraft, and the propulsion systems that get them off the ground.
majors.whyChooseIt: A strong fit for students who love physics and want to work on flight, space exploration, or defense systems, and who don't mind a rigorous, math-heavy curriculum.

majors.name: Mechanical Engineering
majors.summary: One of the broadest engineering majors, covering how physical systems move, generate power, and get manufactured — from engines to robots to consumer products.
majors.whyChooseIt: Good for students who like hands-on building and want maximum flexibility after graduation — mechanical engineers work across nearly every industry.

majors.name: Civil Engineering
majors.summary: Civil engineering trains students to design and build the infrastructure society depends on: roads, bridges, water systems, and buildings.
majors.whyChooseIt: Appeals to students who want to see tangible, lasting results in the world around them and who are interested in a clear path toward professional licensure (PE).

majors.name: Electrical Engineering
majors.summary: Electrical engineering covers the systems that generate, distribute, and control electricity and signals — from microchips to the power grid.
majors.whyChooseIt: A strong choice for students drawn to both hardware and theory, with career paths spanning chips, power, robotics, and communications.

majors.name: Computer Science
majors.summary: Computer science teaches how to design, build, and reason about software systems — the algorithms, data structures, and infrastructure behind modern technology.
majors.whyChooseIt: Great for students who enjoy problem-solving and building things quickly, with some of the widest range of industries hiring straight out of undergrad.

majors.name: Chemical Engineering
majors.summary: Chemical engineering applies chemistry, physics, and math to design the processes that turn raw materials into fuels, chemicals, and pharmaceuticals at scale.
majors.whyChooseIt: Fits students who like chemistry but want to work on large-scale industrial processes rather than lab bench research alone.

majors.name: Statistics / Data Science
majors.summary: This major builds the math, programming, and modeling skills to turn raw data into predictions and decisions.
majors.whyChooseIt: A good fit for students who like math and want it applied to real business or scientific questions rather than pure theory.

majors.name: Biomedical Engineering
majors.summary: Biomedical engineering applies engineering principles to the human body, training students to design medical devices, diagnostics, and health technologies.
majors.whyChooseIt: Ideal for students who want an engineering career with a direct, tangible connection to healthcare and human impact.

majors.name: Biology / Biochemistry
majors.summary: A life-sciences major covering the chemistry and biology of living systems, the standard entry point into bench science and biotech/pharma careers.
majors.whyChooseIt: A natural fit for students who enjoyed high school biology/chemistry and want to work in a lab turning scientific discoveries into real therapies.

majors.name: Public Health
majors.summary: Public health majors study how to protect and improve population-level health through data, policy, and programs, rather than treating individual patients.
majors.whyChooseIt: Good for students who care about health but want to work on prevention and systems-level impact rather than clinical practice.
